reference.source: Robbins Basic Pathology 9th Edition (topic map; text rewritten, no verbatim copy)
clinicalPearls: Aschoff bodies with caterpillar macrophages define rheumatic carditis
Rheumatic vegetations are tiny and non destructive; infective ones destroy and embolise
Staph aureus causes acute endocarditis even on normal valves
Mitral stenosis causes atrial fibrillation and left atrial thrombus
reference.pathophysiology: Molecular mimicry between streptococcal antigens and cardiac proteins triggers pancarditis whose valvular inflammation heals by fibrosis across repeated attacks. In endocarditis, endothelial injury or prosthetic material collects fibrin and platelets that circulating bacteria colonise, protected from immunity inside vegetations that fragment as emboli.
additionalInvestigations: Multiple blood culture sets before antibiotics
Antistreptolysin O and inflammatory markers for rheumatic activity
